checks: Branch scope and ambient types (claim 1). From the k1 premise (isolated u in the disconnected N(v)) plus accepted claim-01, A={u} disjoint-union C with C on 17 vertices, K4-free, alpha(C)=3. I re-derived every partition fact: orders 2+17+17+7=43; vu present and v complete to C, v anticomplete to D union T (=B by definition); u anticomplete to C (isolated component) and to T (=B minus D, since D=N(u) intersect B); u complete to D with d(u)=18 from accepted claim-03(b) (epsilon_u<=d_A(u)=m-1=0, row identity d_B(u)=17+epsilon_u-d_A(u)=17), so |D|=17 and T has 7 vertices, adjacent to neither root. The antineighborhoods are exactly C union T (of u) and D union T (of v); any I4 there plus the root is I5, K5 is excluded by heredity, so both are (5,4)-free of order 24. Neighborhood edge counts are e(C)=e(D)=68, hence deficit 85-68=17 on the published (4,5,18) maximum. No maximum-edge-root or minimum-degree normalization is used anywhere.

Core regularity (claim 1). C: for x in C, N_C(x) is triangle-free (a triangle with x is K4 in the K4-free C) and I4-free (heredity), so R(3,4)=9 gives d_C(x)<=8; for the complement, C-bar is again (4,4)-free, N_{C-bar}(x) is triangle-free (an independent triple among C-nonneighbors of x together with x is an I4 of C) and I4-free (heredity), so d_{C-bar}(x)<=8, i.e. nonneighbors of x in C are at most 8; with d+d_bar=16 every C-degree is exactly 8 and e(C)=68. This is self-contained and matches the recorded (4,4,17) census row 68..68 and reductions 4.4's '17-vertex (4,4) cell is 8-regular'. D: accepted claim-03(b) via the recorded 5.2 trigger (r_u=17 -> 17-vertex 8-regular (4,4) row); D is (4,4)-free by u+K4=K5 and heredity from B. The 'deficit17' figure and both 68-edge neighborhoods recompute exactly.

Budget algebra (claim 2). Re-derived each identity from scratch. Per C-vertex: 9 fixed neighbors (v plus 8 C-neighbors) and edges into D and T, so summing 18+epsilon_c over 17 vertices: 306+E_C = 17 + 136 + r + p, giving r+p = 153+E_C; symmetrically r+q = 153+E_D (u contributes 17 to D). T-vertices touch only C, D, T: p+q+2h = 126+E_T. Fixed edges total 1+34+136 = 171 (vu, 17+17 root-core, 68+68 core-internal), so e(G)=171+r+p+q+h and W=2e(G)-774 = 2(r+p+q+h-216); 43*18=774 checks. Cross edges: x_v = e({u}+C, D+T) = 17+r+p = 170+E_C, x_u = 17+r+q = 170+E_D. All six identities and their constants verified.

Census directions and seven-cell arithmetic (claim 2). Both antineighborhoods are (5,4)-free of order 24, so the recorded interval applies in both directions: 144<=68+p+h<=160 gives 76<=p+h<=92, likewise 76<=q+h<=92; summing lower bounds gives p+q+2h>=152. The upper 168 uses the global degree cap 24 on the seven T-vertices (4.1), stronger than the census upper end (which would give 184) - direction choice correct. Then p+q+2h = 126+E_T in [152,168] gives 26<=E_T<=42, and sum_T(24-d(t)) = 42-E_T <= 16; each summand is nonnegative by 4.1. Lower/upper ends of [144,160] are recorded min/max over all graphs in R(5,4,24) (README semantics, complement cross-check 276-132=144), so both uses are licensed.

Degree-bound uses (all claims). The 18..24 range comes from R(4,5)=25 via reductions 4.1 and is applied exactly where declared: 168 = 7*24; 9<=d_D(c)+d_T(c) from d(c)>=18 (d(c)=9+d_D+d_T) and <=15 from d(c)<=24; nonnegativity of each 24-d(t) deficit. Claim 1 uses only the row cap r_u<=17 (5.2, via claim-03) and R(3,4)=9. The equivalence sentence 'global degree bounds follow' is also correct standalone: d(z)<=17 leaves 25+ nonneighbors containing K4 or I5 by R(4,5)=25 (K4 plus z is K5); d(z)>=25 makes the neighborhood contain K4 or I5 - both contradict K5/I5-freeness, so 18<=d<=24 needs no extra premise.

Attachment inequalities (claim 2). For t in T: S=C-N_C(t) has no I3 (with t and u - pairwise nonadjacent, t,u nonadjacent - an I3 would extend to I5) and is K4-free (heredity from C), so R(4,3)=9 (orientation: any 9-vertex graph has K4 or I3) gives |S|<=8 and |N_C(t)|>=9; the D/v exchange is exact (v is anticomplete to D union T). For c in C: common nonneighbors of the nonedge uc are precisely the 8 C-nonneighbors of c (u is anticomplete to all C) plus T-N_T(c) - D vertices are adjacent to u, v is adjacent to both - of order 15-d_T(c). This set has no I3 (with nonadjacent u,c gives I5) and no K5 (heredity), so it has order at most 13: applying R(5,3)=14 (same recorded value as R(3,5)=14 by classical symmetry; equivalently the cited 4.4 nonedge bound verbatim, or the same number to the complement). Hence d_T(c)>=2, and d_T(c)<=7 because |T|=7; the [9,15] window for d_D(c)+d_T(c) follows from the caps as checked above. The v/d side is the exact mirror.

Root-containing 5-sets (claim 3). Re-derived for every assembled graph under the fixed root incidences: a K5 with v needs a K4 inside N(v)={u}+C, impossible (u isolated in A, C K4-free); with u needs a K4 inside {v}+D, impossible (v anticomplete to D, D K4-free); with both roots needs 3 common neighbors of v,u but N(v) intersect N(u)=empty. An I5 with v needs an I4 inside the antineighborhood D union T, an I5 with u needs one inside C union T - both (5,4)-free by admissibility; with both roots impossible since v,u are adjacent. So no root-containing 5-set can obstruct, independent of X - the a,b>=1 restriction on rootless obstructions is then forced by side validity, exactly as the proof states.

Clique family necessity and sufficiency (claim 3). A rootless K5 lies in C union D union T; it cannot lie in C union T or D union T (side K5-freeness), so it meets both cores, and each core's K4-freeness caps its count at 3. The triples a+b+c=5 with 1<=a<=3, 1<=b<=3, c>=0 are exactly the 8 listed (a,b): (1,1,3),(1,2,2),(1,3,1),(2,1,2),(2,2,1),(2,3,0),(3,1,1),(3,2,0); (3,3,-1) correctly excluded - the list matches line-for-line. For an eligible selection (U internally complete, V internally complete, W internally complete, all U-W in P, all V-W in Q), the only unfixed edges of the prospective K5 are the U x V rectangle, so the single all-one condition is exactly the variable part: necessity (any K5 trips its type's clause) and sufficiency (a violated clause exhibits an explicit K5) both hold; conversely any all-one rectangle on an eligible selection is a K5. Clause lengths recompute to {1,2,3,4,6} for negatives and {4,6} for positives; the triangle sentence is precisely the (1,1,3) clause.

Independent family necessity and sufficiency (claim 3). For a rootless I5 with counts (a,b,c): any 4 vertices inside C union T or D union T would be a forbidden I4, so a+c<=3 and b+c<=3; adding gives 5+c<=6, hence c<=1, and (with a,b>=1, themselves forced since b+c<=3<5 etc.) c=0 leaves exactly (3,2),(2,3) and c=1 forces (2,2) - the 3 listed types are exactly the solutions. For an eligible selection (U,V,W internally independent, all U-W and V-W attachments absent), the only unfixed condition is the all-zero U x V rectangle, so the OR-of-X clause is exactly its negation: necessity (any I5 trips its type's clause) and sufficiency (a violated clause exhibits an explicit I5) both hold. Equivalence domain: sufficiency reads over admissible keys - side (5,4)-freeness and core (4,4)-freeness are load-bearing (a K5 inside C union T would otherwise evade all clauses) and are stated in the sibling admissible_keys field, with the proof itself invoking them ('by side validity'); I record this as the intended and stated quantifier, not a gap.

Coverage and disjointness (claim 3). For a fixed labelled candidate the cell partition is determined (u unique; C=N(v)-{u}; D=N(u)-{v}; T=rest) and extracting (C-graph, D-graph, T-graph, P, Q) yields exactly one key, so different keys are disjoint labelled cases and every candidate sits under exactly one key per within-cell labelling - the scope correctly retains all labelings and asserts no automorphism quotient. Uniqueness of u: claim-01 gives exactly two components and C is 8-regular (no isolated vertex inside C); the corrected line-80 argument is also valid (two components of an 8-regular C would each have >=9 vertices, >=18>17). All edges are accounted for across the five key components plus the 289 X bits (no unspecified edge remains).

Grep of research.json for SRG/strongly/unique/catalogue/complete: no strong-regularity inference anywhere (reductions 12.2's rejection respected; the 8-regularity actually proved); uniqueness of the 17-vertex core and catalogue completeness are explicitly disclaimed ('No catalogue completeness or uniqueness ... is required', 'the existing catalogue filter only gives existence of some D subset B', 'no converse claim for ... the 134112 B-catalogue survivors', matching the catalogue report's own limits). findings.title: Resolved pre-review: inverted component-size inequality at line 80 (preserved)
findings.body: Preserved at the coordinating agent's request. At the pre-correction revision e49eb918... the exact-partition proof read 'if C had two components, each must have at most8 vertices since each vertex has8 internal neighbors' - an inverted deduction: 8 internal neighbors per vertex forces each component to have at least 9 vertices, not at most 8. I caught this in my first independent read; the author corrected the line before final review to 'each would have at least9 vertices since each vertex has8 internal neighbors, contradicting order17', which I verified at the reviewed hash (two components then give >=18>17). The uniqueness conclusion was never at risk: accepted claim-01 already makes C a component (hence connected), and C is 8-regular, so no isolated vertex lies inside C. No outstanding action; recorded for provenance.
